hints.title: Give the repeated expressions short names
hints.body: Put X=2x and Y=log2y. Rewrite the two equations using X and Y.
hints.recap: Use a new variable for a repeated expression, and keep its domain restriction.
hints.pitfall: Keep the range of X and the domain restriction on y beside your equations.
hints.pause: Write the simpler simultaneous equations and the allowed values of X.

recall.reminder: Use a new variable for a repeated expression, and keep its domain restriction.

hints.title: Subtract the equations
hints.body: Eliminate Y by subtracting one equation from the other. Before dividing, check when its remaining coefficient is zero.
hints.recap: Subtracting equations can eliminate a repeated term; a zero coefficient needs separate checking.
hints.pitfall: Not every real value of X can equal an exponential.
hints.pause: Find which values of p give an allowed X.

recall.reminder: Subtracting equations can eliminate a repeated term; a zero coefficient needs separate checking.

hints.title: Check that x and y can be recovered
hints.body: Use your X to find Y. Then undo X=2x and Y=log2y.
hints.recap: Logarithms undo exponentials, but the argument of a real logarithm must be positive.
hints.pitfall: A restriction found by elimination must also give a solution to the original equations.
hints.pause: Check both original equations and state the complete range of p.

recall.reminder: Logarithms undo exponentials, but the argument of a real logarithm must be positive.

solution:
1. Substitute with the ranges attached. Set X=2x>0 and Y=log2y. Since y>0, the variable Y can take any real value.

2. Eliminate Y. Subtracting X+Y=1 from pX+Y=2 gives (p−1)X=1. No solution exists for p=1. Otherwise X=1p−1.

3. Enforce the exponential range. We require X>0, so necessarily p>1.

4. Verify sufficiency. For any p>1, choose X=1p−1 and Y=1−X. The values x=log2X and y=2Y>0 recover a real solution of both original equations.

The complete range is p>1: C.
knowledgePattern: Solve a linearised system while enforcing exponential positivity
